chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “Is there zakat upon the Imam?”

So he عليه السلام said: “You have spoken of an impossibility, O Abu Muhammad. Do you not know that the world and the Hereafter belong to the Imam? He places it wherever he wills and gives it to whomever he wills. That is permissible for him from Allah. Indeed, the Imam, O Abu Muhammad, never passes a night at all except that there is in his neck a right of Allah about which He will question him.”

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the present world and its domain of disposal
key_terms.الْآخِرَةَ: the Hereafter, mentioned here as belonging to the Imam by divine grant
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed Imam, vested with authority and responsibility
key_terms.حَقٌّ: a binding right or claim owed to Allah
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: zakat, the prescribed alms-tax being asked about here
key_terms.يَسْأَلُهُ: He will question him, indicating accountability

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory upon the Imam in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the Imam’s unique divinely granted authority over the world and the Hereafter, affirming that ordinary financial obligations such as zakat are not applied to him in the usual sense. It also emphasizes that this authority is inseparable from responsibility before Allah, as the Imam constantly bears a divine trust for which he is accountable.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah Al Razy, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to himasws, ‘Is there any Zakāt upon the Imamasws?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You have spoken an impossibility, O Abu Muhammad! Do you not know that the world and the Hereafter is for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>? He<sup>asws</sup> can place it wherever he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to and hands it over to whoever he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to. That is allowed for him<sup>asws</sup> from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. The Imam<sup>asws</sup>, O Abu Muhammad, does not sleep at night, ever, and in his<sup>asws</sup> neck is a Right of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Asking him<sup>asws</sup> about it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu ‘Abdallah al-Razi from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamza from his father from abu Basir who has said the following.

“Once I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘Is there any Zakat on Imam?’” He said, “O abu Muhammad, you have spoken an impossible word. Do you not know that both this and the next world belong to the Imam? He can place them as he may want or give them to whoever he may want. It is permissible for him from Allah.
The Imam said, O abu Muhammad, the Imam never spends a night without Allah‘s right on him for which He would not ask him.”
